text:
Ravi: quick question — if a tenant has Dedicated capacity but their pool is saturated, what's our expected behavior for routing to Hosted? Do we allow automatic fallback for premium customers? :thinking:
Ava: short answer: depends on tenant policy. we currently have three modes: "isolate" (never fallback), "best-effort" (fallback to hosted-compatible variant), and "degraded" (fallback but with throttling). need to align console UX.
Chris: Also need to consider model variant compatibility. If dedicated runs quantized int8 variant and hosted has fp16, quality/regression risk.
Jin: +1. Suggest we introduce a per-tenant flag: allow_hosted_fallback { true|false } and a severity level: {silent, warn, block}.
Maria: console should show both a rollout-level toggle and a tenant-level override. UX: tooltip explains quality and PII boundaries. audit log entry whenever fallback occurs.
Ravi: makes sense. how do we enforce data boundaries when falling back to hosted? some customers require no egress.
Ava: for "isolate" tenants we must never route to hosted; for "best-effort" tenants we can if the routing policy detects compatible model variant AND the tenant's egress policy allows it. routing decision tree needs to consult tenant.metadata.egress_allowed and model.compatibility_score.
Chris: can we add a preflight check to avoid noisy failures? something like a quick capability check that returns {compatible: bool, reason: str} before routing.
Jin: example policy snippet:
```
route_policy:
  - name: dedicated_primary
    if: tenant.pool_available > 0
    then: route_to: dedicated
  - name: hosted_fallback
    if: tenant.allow_hosted_fallback == true && tenant.egress_allowed == true && model.compatibility_score >= 0.8
    then: route_to: hosted_variant
  - name: fail_closed
    then: respond: 429
```
Maria: From telemetry POV we need signals on: fallback_rate per-tenant, latency_delta (hosted vs dedicated), quality_delta (sampled prompts), and security_audit_count. Add dashboard tiles and alerts if fallback_rate > X%.
Ravi: how about quotas? if hosted fallback happens, should usage count against dedicated reserved units or fall back to hosted billing?
Ava: billing must reflect actual backend. fallback to hosted should bill hosted units. But console should present an estimated blended cost lens and a toggle to "charge dedicated credits for shortfall" for enterprise deals.
Chris: internal API debate: do we mutate the request to indicate fallback origin (x-served-from: hosted|dedicated)? That helps tracing but might leak to downstream apps.
Jin: add header `x-internal-routing` which is stripped by gateway before returning to customer. trace id linking in logs.
Maria: for rollouts UX: add a canary switch to test fallback in a shadow mode (simulate routing decision and log but don't actually reroute). helps validate before flipping tenant-level toggles.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: routing-policy-service v2.4 will include tenant flag, preflight check endpoint, and telemetry events. ETA: next week.
deploy-bot: rollout plan posted: https://redwood-internal/infra/routing/v2.4 — rolling deploy to canary then prod.
Ravi: next steps: 1) PR for policy evaluation logic (Chris), 2) console toggle + tooltip copy (Maria), 3) preflight endpoint (Jin), 4) telemetry dashboards and alerts (Maria), 5) billing clarifications (FinOps). I'll create tracker.
Ava: LGTM. please add a sample event schema for telemetry so we can instrument quickly.
Chris: will open PR today. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
